newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT -- Bullish dlr/mark cautious after retreat.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT -- Bullish dlr/mark cautious after retreat.

text.p: Dollar/mark's swift decline, after travelling above 1.74 on Friday, did not extinguish its postive bias, though analysts said they could start talking about a bearish double top if the dollar stumbles badly.

"The fact that we traded below 1.73 marks, after failing on the retest of 1.7420 on Friday, leaves a potential double-top. But we have to go quite a bit lower to confirm that pattern," said Pete Grant, senior technical analyst at MMS International.
The dollar's advance to 1.7407 marks on Friday came within a whisker of recapturing the June 6, 39-month high at 1.7423.
Those two tops represented short-term resistance for dollar/mark, analysts said.
But while the rally faltered quickly, the uptrend has not yet been invalidated, chartists said.
Analysts, however, said a break below support at Monday's low of 1.7280 marks would suggest a deeper pullback to the next support around 1.72 marks.

"On the other hand, the move up from 1.7010 marks looked a little impulsive. So, to me this will be just a short-lived correction," said Martin Autotte, technical analyst at CIBC Wood Gundy. "I'm thinking it's going to hold 1.7280 marks."
Below 1.7280 marks, support lies at 1.7190/00 and then around the June 9 bottom at 1.7020, from where the dollar commenced its four-day climb to 1.7407.
Meanwhile, dollar/yen held below it's 21-day moving average resistance line near 115 on Friday, and analysts said that barrier may have thwarted the abrubt rally off 110.65 last week.

"My target is 113.10 yen. That was previous resistance and I think it's going to offer support this time around," said Autotte. "Penetration of that will bring us to 112 yen but I don't see us moving below 112 at this point."
Support between 112 and 110.65 yen looks solid, analysts said.
But Grant said he was pretty confident that if dollar/yen breaks below 113, a retest of 110.65 will follow.
At 1145 EDT on Monday, the dollar was trading at 1.7301/05 marks, off slightly from 1.7310/20 at the open and at 113.39/49 yen, off from 113.66/71.
